## Historically red-lined neighborhoods in LA

```{r}
#1. Create a map of historically red-lined neighborhoods, colored by HOLC grade
# Load data
# Assignments\EDS223-HW2\data\mapping-inequality\mapping-inequality-new-haven.json
la_map <- st_read('Assignments/EDS223-HW2/data/mapping-inequality/mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json')
la_ej <- st_read('Assignments/EDS223-HW2/data/ejscreen/EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb') |> filter(CNTY_NAME == 'Los Angeles County')

crashes <- st_read('Assignments/EDS223-HW2/data/SWITRS_LA/Crashes.csv')

# Check crs: WGS 84
st_crs(la_map)

#Identify columns
colnames(la_map)
length(unique(la_map$grade))
unique(la_map$grade)
nrow(la_map)


#Map it
tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
tm_shape(la_map) +
    tm_polygons(fill = 'grade',
        fill.scale = tm_scale(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2')), 
       fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "HOLC Grade")) +
tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_in("right", "top")) +
tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in('right', 'bottom')) +
tm_legend(position = tm_pos_out('right', 'center')) +
tm_layout(
    main.title = 'Historical Redlining in Los Angeles County (HOLC ranking)'
)
```


```{r}
# Summary table of % census block groups within and outide of each HOLC grade

# Join holc data and ej data
### ej data has census block FIPs Code in ID column
### Test if the LA HOLC data contains FIPS Codes in "area_ID"
nrow(la_map)
length(unique(la_map$area_id))
### Check if reference systems match
if(st_crs(la_map) == st_crs(la_ej)){
  print('File coordinate reference systems match')
} else{
  warning('File coordinate reference systems do not match.  Transform one file before joining')
}

# Transform la_ej to match la_mpa
ej_transformed <- st_transform(la_ej, crs = st_crs(la_map))
# Check whether census blocks overlap
if (any(st_intersects(la_map, ej_transformed, sparse = FALSE))){
  print('census blocks overlap')
} else {
  print("census blocks do not overlap")
}

sf_use_s2(FALSE)
# Join files
holc_ej <- st_join(y = la_map, x = ej_transformed,  join = st_within, left = TRUE) |> st_drop_geometry()

#Confirm join success
if (nrow(holc_ej) == nrow(ej_transformed)){
  print('Join was successful: all census blocks included')
} else {
  print("join failed.")
  print(paste('holc_ej has', nrow(holc_ej), 'rows'))
  print(paste('ej_transformed has ',nrow(ej_transformed), 'rows'))
}

# Create a table summarizing
### percent of census blocks sithin each HOLC grade
### percent of cencus blocks that don't fall within a census grade

# Check number of graded rows in the joined data ()

holc_ej |> group_by(grade) |> summarize(
    Percent = ((n()/nrow(holc_ej))*100)
) |> knitr::kable(col.names = c("HOLC Grade", "Percent of Census Blocks"))


```
 ## Current Conditions by HOLC Grades


```{r}
# Percent Low Income
holc_ej |> group_by(grade) |> drop_na(LOWINCPCT)|> summarize(low_inc_pct = mean(LOWINCPCT)) |> ggplot(
    mapping  = aes(x = grade, y = low_inc_pct, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2', 'lightgray'), name = 'HOLC Ranking') +
    xlab("HOLC Grade") +
    ylab("Percent Low Income Population") +
    ggtitle("Mean Proportion of Low-Income Residents by HOLC Grade") +
    theme_minimal()

# Percentile for PM2.5
# Check why NAs dropped
holc_ej |> group_by(grade) |> drop_na(P_PM25)|> summarize(pm25_percentile = mean(P_PM25, drop_na = TRUE)) |> ggplot(
    mapping  = aes(x = grade, y = pm25_percentile, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2', 'lightgray'), name = 'HOLC Ranking') +
        xlab("HOLC Grade") +
    ylab("Percentile") +
    ggtitle("Mean National Percentile Ranking for Exposure to fine inhalable Air Pollutants (PM2.5) by HOLC Grade") +
    theme_minimal()

# Percentile for Low Life Expectancy
holc_ej |> group_by(grade) |> drop_na(P_LIFEEXPPCT)|> summarize(lowlifeexp_percentile = mean(P_LIFEEXPPCT)) |> ggplot(
    mapping  = aes(x = grade, y = lowlifeexp_percentile, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2', 'lightgray'), name = 'HOLC Ranking') +
    xlab("HOLC Grade") +
    ylab("Percentile") +
    ggtitle("Mean National Percentile Ranking for Low Life Expectancy by HOLC Grade") +
    theme_minimal()
```

On average, areas that received an HOLC grade of C and D currently have a greater proportion of people with low incomes, greater exposure to air pollutants, and have a  lower life expectancy.  30% of census blocks in Los Angeles county are located in areas that received a grade of C or D.  Those census have a disporptionately higher population of low-income residents, at just over 40% of their population. They rank over the 80th national percentile in exposure to fine inhabalble air particles and just under the 60th percentile for low life expectancy; they experience more air pollution of fine particles than 80% of cencus blocks across the US and lower life expectancy than 60%.  In contrast, in areas that recieved a grade of A (just over 1% of LA county's census blocks), less that 20% of the population is low-income.  Areas that recieved an A still rank in the 60th percentile for fine air particle exposure, but just over the 20th percentile for life-expectancy.  This indicates that the NEW DEAL HOLC ranking system has resulted in measurable demographic differences decades later.  Diversion of investments from these areas likely contributes to current disparities in wealth and environmental safety as redlined areas received less real estate investment and resulting social, safety, and  environmental investment.  Lower wealth and greater environmental health risks likely combine with other socioeconmic factors to create the observed disparity in life expectancy. 

## Part 2: Legacy of redlining in pedstrian and bike accidents

```{r}
#Check NAs in Lattitude/Longitude vs Point_X/Point_Y
nrow(crashes)
nrow(crashes['LONGITUDE'] == "NA")
nrow(crashes[crashes['POINT_X'] == "NA"])
sum(is.na(crashes$LATITUDE))
sum(is.na(crashes$POINT_X))

crashes |> summarize_all(~sum(is.na(.)))
colnames(crashes)

crashes |> filter(crashes['LONGITUDE'] == "NA") |> dim()
# Missing data for 97350 rows
crashes |> filter(crashes['POINT_X'] == "NA") |> dim()
# Missing data for 9484 rows
crashes_points <- crashes |> select(-c('LATITUDE', 'LONGITUDE'))
dim(crashes_points)
dim(crashes)

#Conver to geometry class
crashes_spatial <- crashes_points |> mutate(
    POINT_X_numeric = as.numeric(POINT_X),
    POINT_Y_numeric = as.numeric(POINT_Y)
    )|> drop_na(
        POINT_Y_numeric, POINT_X_numeric
    ) |> st_as_sf(
        coords = c('POINT_X_numeric', 'POINT_Y_numeric'),
        crs = 4326)

#Check CRS
if(st_crs(crashes_spatial) == st_crs(la_map)){
  print('File coordinate reference systems match')
} else{
  warning('File coordinate reference systems do not match.  Transform one file before joining')
}

# Transform crs to match joined holc_ej
crashes_transformed <- st_transform(crashes_spatial, crs = st_crs(la_map))

#Confirm CRS change
if(st_crs(crashes_spatial) == st_crs(la_map)){
  print('File coordinate reference systems match')
} else{
  warning('File coordinate reference systems do not match.  Transform one file before joining')
}

#Join with HOLC data
crashes_holc <- st_join(y = la_map, x = crashes_transformed,  join = st_intersects, left = TRUE) |> st_drop_geometry()

#Confirm join success
if (nrow(crashes_holc) == nrow(crashes_transformed)){
  print('Join was successful: all crashes included')
} else {
  print("join failed.")
  print(paste('crashes_holc has', nrow(crashes_holc), 'rows'))
  print(paste('crashes_transformed has ',nrow(crashes_transformed), 'rows'))
}

#Summarize bike/pedestrain crash trends by HOLC grade
crashes_bike_ped <- crashes_holc |> filter(BICYCLE_ACCIDENT == "Y" |
    PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT == "Y") |> drop_na(grade)
crashes_bike_ped |> group_by(grade
    ) |> summarize(percent = n()/nrow(crashes_bike_ped) *100
    ) |> ggplot(
    mapping  = aes(x = grade, y = percent, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2', 'lightgray'),
    name = "HOLC Ranking") +
    xlab("HOLC Grade") +
    ylab("Percent of Crashes") +
    ggtitle("Percentage of bicycle and pedestrian \ncrashes in LA County by location HOLC ranking") +
    theme_minimal()
```

Pedestrian and cyclist safety appears to follow similar patterns with HOLC ranking as income and air pollution, likely contributing to the disparity in life expectancy.  Among areas that received an HOLC ranking, less than 5% of crashes occur in areas with a ranking of A, but over 60% occur in areas wth rankings of C and nearly 30% in areas ranked as D. This likely resulted from less investment in safety infrastcure and maintenance in these historically lower-income areas, especially if hazard reporting, funding, and response times are influenced by income and demographic factors.  To strategically improve pedestrian and cyclist safety, the County of LA can invest in more safety measures in historically redlined areas and critically examine how it makes decisions related to safety infrastructure investment and maintenance.
